description: What a mailbox message sent to a head on another machine carries and where it is refused. The stream and its two types are registered in event-streams.v1.json (stream project:mailbox, one scope per type, never changed). This file is the text the sender checks at send time and the receiver checks at ingest; a number here is a limit in force, not a plan figure. A body over the cap is refused, never cut. Bodies are plaintext in the Git remote for good.

payload.meaning: message id, unique per signer machine; the dedupe key is (signer machine, id)
sender's full session id and machine id; the receiver derives the frame handle from the verified id, never from payload text
recipient's full session id (as published in the shared directory) and machine id
message kind as the same-machine mailbox defines it
UTF-8 text, at most limits.maxBodyBytes bytes
full id of the message this one answers
display only; never used to order, age or dedupe a message
signature of the canonical payload under the signing domain, by the sender machine's key

wakeVersion.when: only a send that asks for a wake (`fgos mailbox send --wake`); every other send stays version 1 under the domain above, byte for byte, so a receiver that does not know version 2 still takes plain mail

adds.meaning: the sender asks for the recipient's session to be woken; the receiver decides, under its own limits, whether it takes effect, and never wakes for a machine whose key is not confirmed

wakeVersion.olderReaders: a receiver that does not know version 2 drops the event at its shape check with the counted reason remote-malformed; it never takes the message without its wake flag

bodyRefVersion.when: the body leaves the event: the sender writes it to its mail-body ref and signs a header that names it. Receivers take version 3 before any sender writes it

adds.meaning: sha256 of the body bytes; also the name of the blob that holds the body
length of the body in bytes, at most limits.maxBodyBytes

bodyRefVersion.keeps: every other field of version 1; `wake`, when present, is `true` and is signed in this same domain, so a wake needs no second domain
bodyRefVersion.bodyHome: the tree of the tip of the sender machine's mail-body ref, as this clone mirrors it at refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/mail-bodies/<sender machine>: one blob per message, named bodyHash, holding the body bytes

receiverStates.delivered: the blob is there, sha256 of its bytes equals bodyHash and its length equals bodyBytes: the message is taken exactly like a version 1 or 2 message with that body
receiverStates.expired: the blob is absent after a body fetch that started after this sync's event fetch succeeded, on a clone that has the mail-body fetch mapping: the message is not delivered and the receiver settles it as refused with reason remote-body-expired
receiverStates.held: the blob is absent and that fetch condition does not hold (the clone lacks the mail-body fetch mapping, the body fetch or the event sync failed, or a Git read failed): the receiver settles nothing and sends no refusal, and the cursor for the sender's store origin stops before the message, so the next sync reads it again; later mail of that origin is taken meanwhile and read again without being taken twice, because a message is taken once by (machine, id). A hold ends when the message is delivered, or is dropped as remote-stale once its age passes mailbox.remote.maxAgeSec plus the skew tolerance, so a clone that never gets the mapping holds it for at most that long. The sender sees no refusal during a hold: its status keeps counting the message as waiting, and when the hold ends in remote-stale no settlement is signed either, so the message stays waiting as unanswered, the same as mail that never arrived
receiverStates.malformed: the blob is there but its hash, length or UTF-8 is wrong, or the name is not a blob: dropped with the counted reason remote-malformed, never delivered

bodyRefVersion.olderReaders: a receiver that does not know version 3 drops the event at its shape check with the counted reason remote-malformed

payload.meaning: id of the message being settled
receiver to sender; without it a refusal on the receiver cannot reach the sender
refusal reason code, same codes as the same-machine mailbox
signature under the settled signing domain

limits.enforcedAt: send: the sender refuses a larger body and does not cut it; ingest: the receiver drops an event whose body is larger, counted
limits.source: owner-approved V8 plan; lead:ES accepted the figure 2026-10-28

limits.enforcedAt: ingest: an event older than this by the receiver's clock, less skew tolerance, is dropped with a counted reason
ingest: tolerance when ageing an event; measured skew between two machines was 0.77 s on 2026-10-28
ingest: only a machine whose key pin is confirmed is accepted; a seen or re-keyed machine is dropped and counted

refusalsToSender.meaning: a version 3 message whose body is no longer in the sender's mail-body ref, as found by a body fetch of this sync; the header is all that is left, so the message is not delivered
the message was in the shared log before this machine's first ingest, which takes a baseline and delivers nothing older; the receiver answers it at that ingest so the sender stops waiting

perSenderCaps.accountedBy: verified signer machine and sender id; never the shared unregistered bucket
perSenderCaps.meaning: the same-machine caps of limits.v1.json apply unchanged to each remote sender; its wake budget is its own and smaller (mailbox.wake.remoteLifetimeCap), never the exemption a sender with no head has
